rounds.text: Chiraharit Ltd trades at a staggering price-to-earnings multiple of 108 [E1], demanding a massive growth premium that is completely unsupported by its operational reality. The company delivers a negligible return on equity of 1.18% [E7] and an anemic return on capital employed of 3.59% [E8], both of which severely underperform the respective sector benchmarks of 19.15% [E7] and 19% [E8]. This catastrophic deterioration in profitability is underscored by a recent one-year median return on equity of just 2% [E19], aligning directly with screen reasons highlighting this low 2% ROE [E44]. Furthermore, investors receive zero income support while waiting for a turnaround, as the dividend yield sits firmly at 0.00% [E4]. However, these historical metrics mask the severe present-day collapse in capital efficiency that renders the current 108x valuation entirely unjustifiable [E1, E19].
